title: Chicken jambalaya
skill: The trinity, deglazing, rice cooked in the pot

notes.text: For more than 6, brown the chicken in two batches, and make sure the rice and broth fill your pot no more than halfway.

callback.body: When you made adobo, the brown bits left stuck in the pot melted into the sauce. Those bits have a name, fond, and today you'll get every one of them into the pot on purpose.

move.title: Brown, sweat, deglaze, simmer
move.body: Jambalaya is a one-pot rice dish from Louisiana. Every step builds flavor in the same pot. First you brown sausage and chicken, which leaves brown bits on the bottom. Then you cook the holy trinity, onion, celery, and green pepper, gently until soft. Then you deglaze: pour in broth and scrape the brown bits loose so they melt into it. Last, the rice cooks right in that flavorful broth and soaks it all up.

why.title: The brown bits are flavor
why.body: When meat browns, some of its juices stick to the pot and turn dark brown. That's fond. It looks like a mess, but it's packed with deep, savory flavor. Don't wash it away, and don't let it turn black.

why.title: Sweat the trinity, don't brown it
why.body: Onion, celery, and green pepper are Louisiana's holy trinity, the start of many Cajun and Creole dishes. Here you cook them on medium, stirring, until they're soft and sweet. That's sweating. The water that comes out of them starts loosening the fond.

why.title: Deglaze to lift it all up
why.body: Pour a little broth into the hot pot and it sizzles and steams. Scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon and the stuck brown bits dissolve into the broth. Now the rice can soak up all that flavor.

why.title: Lid on, hands off
why.body: Rice cooks in the steam trapped under the lid. Lifting the lid lets the steam escape, and stirring breaks the grains and makes them mushy. Set the timer and leave it alone.

wrong.sign: The rice is still crunchy when the timer rings
wrong.fix: Sprinkle ¼ cup of water over the top, put the lid back on, and cook 5 more minutes on low.

wrong.sign: It smells scorched on the bottom
wrong.fix: Turn off the heat right away. Spoon the top into a bowl and leave the burnt layer in the pot. Next time, use your lowest heat.

wrong.sign: The rice is soggy or mushy
wrong.fix: Leave the lid off for 5 minutes on low so extra water steams away. Next time, don't stir after the lid goes on.

wrong.sign: The fond turned black while browning
wrong.fix: Wipe the black bits out carefully with a paper towel and a little oil before adding the vegetables. Black fond tastes bitter.
Put the lid back on and cook 5 more minutes on low, then check again.

quiz.q: What's the holy trinity in Louisiana cooking?
quiz.explain: Carrot, celery, and onion is the French and Italian base. Louisiana swaps the carrot for green pepper.

quiz.q: Why pour broth in and scrape the bottom of the pot?
choices: To lift the brown bits so their flavor goes into the dish
To clean the pot for later
quiz.explain: That's deglazing. The fond melts into the broth, and the rice soaks it up.

ingredients.prep: low-sodium if you can find it

steps.text: Stir the paprika, oregano, thyme, black pepper, salt, and the cayenne if you're using it together in the small bowl.
Dice the onion, green pepper, celery, and tomatoes, and mince the garlic. Keep the tomatoes and garlic in their own piles.
steps.tip: Make the vegetable pieces about the same size, so they soften at the same rate.

steps.text: Slice the sausage into coins about ¼ inch thick.
steps.tip: Smoked sausage is already cooked, so it doesn't need a wash step. The chicken does.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into pieces about 1 inch across and put them in the mixing bowl. Sprinkle on half the spice mix and toss with your hand until coated.
Wash your hands, the knife, and the cutting board with hot, soapy water.
steps.tip: Raw chicken can carry germs. Wash before you touch anything else.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the large pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the sausage and cook, stirring now and then, until both sides are browned. Lift it out with the slotted spoon onto the plate. Leave the fat and brown bits in the pot.
steps.look: Browned coins and a brown layer starting on the bottom of the pot.

steps.text: Use the tongs to spread the chicken in the pot in one layer.
steps.tip: Lay each piece down away from you, so any spatter goes the other way.

steps.text: Wash your hands, and wash the mixing bowl with hot, soapy water.
Leave the chicken alone until it's browned underneath, then turn the pieces and brown the other side. Move it to the plate with the sausage. It won't be cooked through yet.
steps.look: Golden brown chicken, and a darker brown layer on the bottom of the pot, but nothing black.

steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion, green pepper, and celery and cook, stirring often, until they're soft. Scrape at the bottom as you stir.
Add the garlic, the tomato paste, and the rest of the spice mix. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in 1 cup of the broth. It will sizzle. Deglaze the pot: scrape the bottom with the wooden spoon until all the brown bits come loose and the bottom feels smooth.
steps.tip: Pour the broth in slowly and keep your face back from the steam.
steps.look: The bottom of the pot is clean, and the broth has turned brown.

steps.text: Stir in the rice for 1 minute, until every grain is coated. Pour in the rest of the broth, and add the tomatoes and bay leaves. Put the sausage and chicken back in, with any juice on the plate.
Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil. Give it one good stir so no rice is stuck to the bottom.
steps.look: Big bubbles all over the top.

steps.text: Turn the heat to low, put the lid on, and let it cook without lifting the lid or stirring.

Lift the lid away from you. Taste a few grains from the top with a clean fork. They should be tender, and the broth soaked up. If the rice is still crunchy, sprinkle ¼ cup of water over it, cover, and cook 5 more minutes.
steps.tip: Tip the lid away from you so the steam rises on the far side.

steps.text: Slide the thermometer into the thickest piece of chicken. It needs to read at least 165°F. If it doesn't, cover it and cook 5 more minutes on low, then check again.
Turn off the stove and put the lid back on. Let it rest so the rice finishes steaming.
Fish out the bay leaves and throw them away. Fluff the jambalaya gently with the fork, and serve it with the green onions on top if you're using them.
steps.tip: Bay leaves stay stiff and sharp even after cooking, so nobody should eat them.
